chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the amulet that is hung upon the menstruating woman. He said: 'Yes, there is no problem.'
He said, and he said: 'She can recite it and write it, and her hand does not touch it.' And it is reported that she does not write the Quran.

key_terms.التَّعْوِيذِ: Amulet or charm containing Quranic verses or prayers
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a menstruating woman to wear an amulet or recite Quranic verses?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the permissibility of a menstruating woman using an amulet (ta'widh) containing Quranic verses, resolving the tension between the general prohibition of reciting Quran while impure and the specific allowance for healing or protection. It distinguishes between the act of recitation and the physical handling, noting that while she may write the text, some reports suggest she should avoid direct contact with the Quranic script itself, reflecting the nuanced juristic approach to ritual purity (taharah) in Shia fiqh. The ruling underscores the practical application of Quranic verses in daily life, even during states of minor or major impurity, provided the content is treated with respect.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Dawood Bin Farqad, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the amulet hanging upon the menstruating woman.
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, there is no problem’.
He (the narrator) said, ‘And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘She can recite it and write it, but her hand cannot touch it’. And it is reported that she cannot write the Quran.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Dawud ibn Farqad who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of al-Ta‘widh (protective sacred expressions from Quran or names of Allah) which women hang on themselves. He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, it is not harmful.’
He (the Imam) said, ‘She can read, write but must not touch.’ It is narrated that she cannot write al-Quran.’”
